findings.title: Missing optional chaining causes crash when no destinationCalendar exists
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` will throw a TypeError ("Cannot read properties of undefined") whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is empty/null and the booking location is Google Meet. This is a very common scenario (organizer/host has no connected calendar), and since this code runs inside `EventManager.create()`, which is invoked on every booking, this will crash booking creation for any Google-Meet booking without a destination calendar. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`, which was safe; the refactor to an array dropped the optional chaining on the destructured element.

findings.title: Inverted condition for setting organization slug breaks org creation
findings.body: The condition for assigning `slug` was changed from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, inverting the logic. Combined with the unchanged `requestedSlug` assignment (`...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {})`), when billing is disabled the newly created organization now gets neither `slug` nor `requestedSlug`, so the org has no usable slug at all; when billing is enabled it gets both `slug` and a pending `requestedSlug`, which is contradictory. This change is unrelated to the stated purpose of the PR (destinationCalendar handling) and looks like an accidental regression from a bad merge/rebase that will break organization creation, particularly for self-hosted instances where billing is disabled.

findings.title: Dead fallback logic in updateEvent leaves calendarId undefined
findings.body: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` searches for a destinationCalendar entry whose `externalId` equals `externalCalendarId` — but this branch is only reached when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the comparison `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` can essentially never match. The fallback therefore always resolves to `undefined`, and `calendar.events.update({ calendarId: undefined, ... })` is called, which will fail against the Google Calendar API. This breaks calendar updates whenever `externalCalendarId` isn't already known/stored (e.g. missing/legacy booking references), a case this PR's multi-calendar support is supposed to handle correctly.

findings.title: Same dead fallback logic duplicated in deleteEvent
findings.body: `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` has the identical self-referential bug as in updateEvent: the `.find` predicate compares against the already-known-falsy `externalCalendarId`, so it never matches and always yields `undefined`. Unlike updateEvent, this one is masked by the subsequent `calendarId ? calendarId : defaultCalendarId` fallback to `"primary"`, but it means the code silently falls back to deleting from the primary calendar instead of the correct destination calendar whenever `externalCalendarId` is not supplied, which can delete the wrong event or fail to delete the intended one for secondary host calendars.

findings.title: Hangout link patch call omits the "primary" fallback used for insert
findings.body: In `createEvent`, the `calendar.events.insert` call uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the subsequent `calendar.events.patch` call (to attach the hangout link in the description) uses the raw `calendarId: selectedCalendar` without the same fallback. If no destinationCalendar entry matches the current `credentialId` (so `selectedCalendar` is `undefined`), the insert succeeds against "primary" but the patch call is made with an undefined calendarId, which will fail to update the description with the hangout link.

findings.title: Organizer email override always uses the first destinationCalendar regardless of which host's credential is creating the event
findings.body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is destructured as the first element of `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar` and used to override the organizer attendee's email (`email: mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId : calEventRaw.organizer.email`). When `createAllCalendarEvents` loops over multiple destination calendars/hosts and calls `createEvent` once per host credential, every call still uses the same first-array-entry override instead of the entry matching the `credentialId` actually creating the event (which is correctly looked up a few lines later via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`). As a result, for collective events with multiple hosts, every secondary host's calendar event will show the first host's calendar email as the "organizer" attendee instead of their own, undermining the core fix this PR is meant to deliver. The same bug exists in `updateEvent` (lines 198-230) with `mainHostDestinationCalendar`.

findings.title: Pushing team destination calendars onto evt.destinationCalendar is a no-op when it is null
findings.body: `destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (see the ternary ending in `: null,`). Later, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` uses optional chaining, which silently does nothing when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`. Consequently, for a COLLECTIVE event where the organizer has no personal destination calendar but other hosts do, all the collected `teamDestinationCalendars` are discarded and only the organizer is considered (incorrectly, with none at all), so secondary hosts never get their calendar invites created — defeating the main goal of this PR in exactly the scenario it is meant to fix.

findings.title: organization.slug selection dropped from loadUsers query for dynamic bookings
findings.body: In the refactored `loadUsers` function, the Prisma `select` used for the dynamic/group booking branch (`!eventTypeId`) no longer includes `organization: { select: { slug: true } }`, which was present before this change. If any downstream code in this handler (or in dynamic booking flows generally) relies on `organizerUser.organization?.slug` (e.g., for organization-aware booking links), it will now silently receive `undefined`, changing behavior for dynamic/group bookings tied to an organization without any related test coverage added.

findings.title: Error logging removed from updateAllCalendarEvents failure path
findings.body: The previous `console.error(message)` call in the catch block of `updateAllCalendarEvents` was removed when converting the single-reference return to the multi-reference `.map()` version. Errors that occur while updating calendar events (e.g. missing credentials) are now silently swallowed without any log output, making production issues in this path much harder to diagnose.

findings.title: Inconsistent null vs empty-array representation of "no destination calendar" across code paths
findings.body: This test now expects `destinationCalendar: []` for the BOOKING_REJECTED webhook payload (produced via confirm.handler.ts, which always falls back to `[]`), while the BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED tests in the same file still expect `destinationCalendar: null` (produced via handleNewBooking.ts, which falls back to `null`). Both represent the same "no calendar connected" state but surface differently depending on which code path produced the CalendarEvent. Since `destinationCalendar` is now a public/typed field consumed by webhooks and third-party integrations, this inconsistency (`null` in some flows, `[]` in others) is a fragile and confusing contract that should be normalized to one representation.

findings.title: No tests cover multi-host destinationCalendar behavior introduced by this PR
findings.body: This PR converts `destinationCalendar` from a single object to an array across 22 files and rewrites significant parts of EventManager.ts, CalendarManager.ts, and handleNewBooking.ts's collective-event calendar logic (including the host-list building at this line and the `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)` call), but the author's checklist explicitly states no tests were added, and the only test file touched (webhook.e2e.ts) merely adjusts one assertion to match the new shape rather than verifying the multi-host calendar invite behavior described as the purpose of the PR. Given the number of latent bugs this refactor introduces (e.g. the no-op push when destinationCalendar is null, and the Google Calendar organizer-override/fallback bugs), the lack of any automated test for the actual collective multi-host calendar scenario is a significant gap for a change of this risk level.
